title: Sebastian and the Safehouse
premise: Noor Ravensworth, a whistle-blower living under four names in a Baltic port city, receives a voiceprint ping from a dead colleague's encrypted server, revealing that the evidence he buried years ago has been copied and is being auctioned to the highest bidder. Hunted by the private security firm he exposed and by the broker selling his secret, Noor must reach a safehouse network run by his estranged sister before the checkpoint rotations change at dawn. Along the way he learns the broker is the son of the man whose death Noor's leak caused, seeking justice outside any courtroom. In the end, Noor trades the one secret worth killing for—his own testimony—to the broker in exchange for the copied files, then surrenders himself publicly, choosing accountability over survival.
about_author: F. M. Thackeray is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent a decade writing security briefings before turning to fiction. They live quietly near a border town, which they describe as 'excellent research.'

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Introduces Noor's fragmented life under four identities in Gdansk, his insomnia, and the rituals of invisibility. Emotional beat: brittle control masking chronic fear.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. A dead colleague's server unlocks using an old recording of Noor's voice, delivering a message: 'They have copies.' Emotional beat: dread reawakening after years of dormancy.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. He audits what was leaked, who died, and what could still be out there. Flashback to the incident. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a body in shallow water.

chapters.title: The Man at the Fish Market
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. He spots surveillance that doesn't match police patterns—private contractors. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into certainty.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper Ravensworth, Noor's estranged sister, runs the safehouse network from Rotterdam. She learns someone is asking about her brother. Emotional beat: wary love tangled with resentment.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Rotations
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. He maps the border schedule and realizes he has a narrow window before shifts change and his forged papers fail. Emotional beat: the clock starting.

chapters.title: The Broker
chapters.summary: POV: Elias Marchetti, the broker auctioning the files, revealed as the son of the man killed by Noor's leak. He wants more than money. Emotional beat: cold purpose with grief underneath.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. His third identity is compromised; he burns the apartment and runs with a go-bag. Emotional beat: loss of the last illusion of safety.

chapters.title: Night Train
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. A tense rail journey where a contractor sits two seats away. Emotional beat: stillness as survival, terror held in a held breath.

chapters.title: What Father Left Me
chapters.summary: POV: Elias. Backstory: his father's death, the settlement that bought silence, and how he found the files. Emotional beat: inheritance as wound.

chapters.title: Dead Drop in Rostock
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. He retrieves cash and a burner from an old contact who demands answers. Emotional beat: debts of loyalty coming due.

chapters.title: The Firm
chapters.summary: POV: Contractor team lead Dana Kovač. Her employer—the exposed firm—wants Noor silenced before the auction closes. Emotional beat: professional detachment beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Sister Static
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Noor makes first contact in six years; she refuses him, then relents partially. Emotional beat: anger as armor over fear for him.

chapters.title: The Auction Opens
chapters.summary: POV: Elias. Bidding begins among state actors and corporations; the price climbs past what money can settle. Emotional beat: power curdling into isolation.

chapters.title: Ferry to Rotterdam
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Crossing the North Sea, he deciphers a second message hidden in the server: his own original testimony, unredacted. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as danger.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Noor arrives; the siblings negotiate terms of trust in a basement full of other fugitives' stories. Emotional beat: fragile reunion.

chapters.title: Kovač Closes In
chapters.summary: POV: Dana. She traces the ferry manifest and identifies the safehouse district. Emotional beat: duty versus doubt about her employer's methods.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. He considers buying back the files with the unredacted testimony—but releasing it endangers everyone who helped him once. Emotional beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: House Guest
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. One of her guests is feeding information to Kovač. Small betrayals accumulate. Emotional beat: trust as a structural weakness.

chapters.title: Elias Comes West
chapters.summary: POV: Elias. He flies to Rotterdam personally, tired of proxies, carrying his father's photograph. Emotional beat: obsession becoming pilgrimage.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Kindness
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. The mole is gently cornered at dinner; he confesses—he was protecting a daughter held as leverage. Emotional beat: compassion complicating betrayal.

chapters.title: The Daughter
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. The network mounts an off-book rescue of the mole's child while the house prepares to move. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: POV: Dana. Ordered to raid the safehouse, she delays twelve minutes—the exact time needed for the rescue. Emotional beat: the line crossed, irreversibly.

chapters.title: Empty Rooms
chapters.summary: POV: Kovač's team finds the safehouse stripped clean. Kovač reports failure and resigns mid-operation. Emotional beat: quiet defection.

chapters.title: Meeting Terms
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Through an intermediary, Noor offers Elias a trade: the testimony for the files. Elias counters—he wants Noor, not paper. Emotional beat: bargaining with grief.

chapters.title: What the Files Say
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Reading the auction copy, he discovers it omits the one fact that would exonerate a blamed junior analyst. Emotional beat: responsibility crystallizing.

chapters.title: Vesper's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. She shows Noor every person her network lost doing this work, asking if he understands the cost of going public. Emotional beat: love as hard truth.

chapters.title: The Checkpoint Shifts
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Dawn rotation changes seal the borders; escape routes close one by one. Staying is now the only plan. Emotional beat: claustrophobic finality.

chapters.title: Confession, Drafted
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. He writes the public statement he buried years ago, naming names including his own. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Kovač's Warning
chapters.summary: POV: Dana. Having quit, she warns Noor that the firm's last option is deniable violence tonight. Emotional beat: an enemy becoming an unlikely ally.

chapters.title: The Rooftop Meeting
chapters.summary: POV: Elias and Noor. Face to face above the city: Elias wants a confession on his terms; Noor offers truth on his. Emotional beat: two inheritances colliding.

chapters.title: Handshake
chapters.summary: POV: Elias. He accepts the trade—testimony for the files—and admits revenge never matched the shape of his grief. Emotional beat: mourning finding a better object.

chapters.title: The Firm Moves Early
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Contractors hit the meeting site; flight through the docks with the drive containing everything. Emotional beat: adrenaline stripped to essentials.

chapters.title: Blood on the Quay
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. She takes a bullet shielding Noor during the dock escape; the network's medics save her. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Upload
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. From a hospital-adjacent safe flat, he publishes the testimony, the files, and the firm's records simultaneously worldwide. Emotional beat: point of no return, strangely calm.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Hour One
chapters.summary: POV: Multiple brief cuts—arrests begin, markets wobble, Elias watches his father's name enter the record accurately at last. Emotional beat: consequences unfolding.

chapters.title: Surrender
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. He walks into a federal building with his lawyer and his real name spoken aloud for the first time in years. Emotional beat: relief inside fear.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Testifying, he answers for the death his leak caused without flinching or excusing. Emotional beat: accountability as the only exit.

chapters.title: Sentencing and Settlements
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Noor receives a reduced sentence; the firm collapses; Elias funds the victims' fund anonymously. Emotional beat: imperfect justice, honestly priced.

chapters.title: Sleeping Through the Night
chapters.summary: POV: Noor, epilogue. Years later, visiting Vesper after release, he sleeps eight hours in a guest room above the rebuilt safehouse. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.
